name: Sysco Corporation

profile.description: Sysco Corporation is the world's largest foodservice distribution company, supplying food, smallwares and kitchen equipment to restaurants, healthcare, education and hospitality customers across roughly 90 countries. Fiscal 2026 (ended June 27, 2026) sales reached a record $84.6B (+3.9%) with adjusted EPS of $4.61 (+3.4%), and management guided FY2027 to 6-7% sales growth and 9-11% adjusted EPS growth on a 53-week basis. In March 2026 Sysco agreed to acquire Jetro Restaurant Depot, the cash-and-carry wholesaler with ~167 warehouse stores, for ~$29.1B ($21.6B cash plus 91.5M shares), expected to close by fiscal Q3 2027 pending HSR antitrust clearance. Sysco reports fiscal Q1 2027 results on November 3, 2026.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The core broadline model is little changed in five years, but Sysco has layered on specialty and digital ordering and in March 2026 agreed to a ~$29.1B acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot that would add a cash-and-carry channel serving small independent restaurants [5]; because the deal is still pending HSR review it is not yet a proven new revenue stream, so it earns only partial credit. AI Deployment (2/2): AI is now quantified — FY2027 guidance embeds ~$100M of efficiency gains from an AI-powered transformation of inventory, forecasting, routing and back-office work, the company targets at least $500M of AI-driven efficiency by FY2029, and management credited an AI selling tool with helping penetration outpace the industry in Q4 FY2026 [1][4]. Market Share (2/2): Sysco is the category leader with record $84.6B sales and Q4 FY2026 U.S. Foodservice case volume +2.5% [1][3]. Pipeline (1/2): The $100M FY2027 AI savings and a Restaurant Depot close targeted by fiscal Q3 2027 give dated visibility, but these are efficiency/M&A milestones rather than named next-generation products [1][5]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP reports R&D at 0% of revenue; innovation spending is embedded in operations [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Since May 2021 Sysco has articulated the purpose 'Connecting the world to share food and care for one another,' paired with a mission of 'delivering success for our customers' [9]; it is clearer and more human than a pure commercial slogan, but it is only five years old and the strategy that dominates disclosures (scale, AI efficiency, a $29B debt-funded acquisition) does not visibly flow from it. Community Impact (1/2): The annual global Purpose Month mobilizes colleagues from 339 sites in 9 countries for food-insecurity volunteering, with nearly 17,000 volunteer hours logged in its first year [9] — genuine but general corporate philanthropy without disclosed dollar totals in our sources. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found, and Sysco is operating with an interim CFO (Brandon Sewell) [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP data show a single open-market purchase in Q2 2026 against six open-market sales in Q3 2026 and two in Q1 2026 — net selling, with most acquisitions being equity grants [7].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock on 10 metrics (raw 7.35/10, rounds to 7). Strengths: ROE of 75.5% [2], 5yr revenue CAGR of 10.5% (FY2021 $51.3B to FY2026 $84.6B, flattered by the COVID-depressed base) [2], and a forward P/E of ~16.4 (derived: $82.90 price over FY2027 adjusted EPS of ~$5.07, i.e. FY2026 $4.61 grown at the 10% guidance midpoint) [1][2] all score 1.0, as do 56 years of dividend payments and increases [6]. Revenue growth of 3.9% YoY scores 0.80, payout ratio of 59% scores 0.68, and the 3.7% 5yr dividend CAGR scores 0.62 against the 6% target [2][6]. The drags are debt-to-equity of 561% (0.0) — total debt $13.5B and net debt/adjusted EBITDA of 2.7x before ~$21B of new acquisition debt — and a 2.08% net margin (0.10) [1][2]. Liquidity is far above the floor at ~$300M of average daily turnover (3.62M shares x $82.90).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Sysco's earnings come from physically buying, storing, picking and trucking perishable food to restaurants, hospitals and schools — work no AI model can substitute — and the only analyst AI commentary found frames Sysco's AI program as a competitive warning to other distributors rather than a threat to Sysco [4]. Residual risk is that AI-enabled procurement or marketplaces could narrow the scale advantage or intermediate customer relationships, which keeps this short of 9. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI is clearly productive — ~$100M of FY2027 efficiency, a $500M FY2029 target, and an AI selling tool credited with penetration gains [1][4] — but these are cost savings and an unquantified sales assist, not quantifiable AI revenue, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded.

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens Sysco is a durable but mostly finite-minded operator: a 56-year dividend streak and a 2021 purpose statement about sharing food and caring for one another show some long-horizon intent, yet strategy is expressed chiefly through scale, efficiency targets and a $29B debt-funded acquisition. The purpose is genuine but young and untested, culture evidence is thin, and the company's evolution has been adjacent rather than reinventive.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Connecting the world to share food and care for one another' is service-oriented and idealistic in a way the old mission was not, and leadership operationalizes it through an annual global Purpose Month focused on food insecurity [9]. It has not yet been tested through a crisis or a leadership transition, and investor communications are dominated by EPS, efficiency and M&A rather than the cause, so it sits at 'genuine, partially lived' rather than competitive advantage [1][5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Kevin Hourican has led since 2020 and the board was expanded to 13 with two AI/supply-chain directors in September 2026, signaling governance continuity [4]. However, the finance function is under an interim CFO [6], no retention or tenure data was found, and the AI program is explicitly aimed at changing 'how we execute our day-to-day business' — a large change-management burden for 75,000 associates — so trust is adequate rather than demonstrably high.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Hourican's public case for the Restaurant Depot deal stresses that the two companies serve distinct channels with limited customer overlap rather than talking about crushing US Foods or Performance Food Group [5], and the company's AI messaging frames gains as serving customers better (penetration via an AI selling tool) rather than as a war on rivals [4]. This is a modest but genuine improvement-oriented posture.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Adding a 167-store cash-and-carry wholesaler and committing to a multi-year AI re-engineering of routing, merchandising and sales represent meaningful adaptation of the delivery-based broadline model [4][5]. These moves extend rather than abandon the core business, and the 2015 blocked US Foods merger shows a recurring preference for scale-by-acquisition over reinvention [5].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Sysco kept raising its dividend through COVID and is accepting a large near-term leverage increase plus $54M of rate-lock losses and bridge costs to pursue Restaurant Depot, while funding a multi-year AI program [1][6]. But the deal is debt-financed M&A of the kind Sinek treats skeptically, and no example of exiting a profitable-but-misaligned business was found, so this is a single point rather than a pattern.

investment_thesis: Sysco is the scale leader in foodservice distribution, delivering record FY2026 sales of $84.6B and adjusted EPS of $4.61, and guiding FY2027 to 6-7% sales growth and 9-11% adjusted EPS growth that includes ~$100M of AI-driven efficiency [1]. At ~$82.90 the stock trades at about 16x our derived FY2027 EPS with a 2.63% yield backed by 56 years of dividend increases and a planned $0.04 annual increase for FY2027 [2][6]. The AI program has moved from governance to numbers — a $500M efficiency target by FY2029 and an AI selling tool credited with share gains [4] — and the business is structurally immune to AI substitution. If the ~$29.1B Restaurant Depot acquisition clears HSR review, Sysco adds a higher-margin cash-and-carry channel serving independent operators that is largely complementary to its delivery network [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is balance-sheet and execution risk. Debt-to-equity is already 561% with $13.5B of debt and 2.7x net debt/EBITDA, and the Restaurant Depot deal will be funded with ~$21B of new debt and hybrid debt plus 91.5M new shares (~16% dilution to Jetro holders) [1][5]; a 2.08% net margin leaves little cushion for integration missteps, food inflation or fuel spikes [2]. Antitrust risk is real given the FTC blocked Sysco's 2015 US Foods merger [5]. Near term, consensus expects fiscal Q1 2027 EPS growth of only ~1.7% ($1.17 vs. guidance of $1.18-$1.20) with restaurant traffic softness and fuel and sourcing pressures, leaving the 9-11% full-year target back-half loaded [3]. GAAP EPS actually fell 1.9% in FY2026, the 3.7% 5yr dividend CAGR barely beats inflation, and payout is 59% of GAAP earnings [2][6].
key_catalysts: Fiscal Q1 2027 earnings on November 3, 2026 versus consensus of ~$22.2B revenue and $1.17 EPS and management guidance of $1.18-$1.20 — a beat would de-risk the back-half-weighted 9-11% FY2027 EPS growth target [3]
HSR clearance and closing of the ~$29.1B Jetro Restaurant Depot acquisition, targeted by fiscal Q3 2027, adding ~167 cash-and-carry warehouse stores across 35 states [5]
Delivery of ~$100M of AI-powered efficiency in FY2027 on the path to a $500M+ run-rate by FY2029 across routing, merchandising, inventory and sales [1][4]
key_risks: Leverage: ~$21B of new debt/hybrid debt for Restaurant Depot on top of $13.5B existing debt and 561% D/E could pressure ratings and constrain dividend growth already running at just 3.7% per year [1][2][5]

Antitrust: the FTC blocked Sysco's 2015 US Foods merger; an extended HSR review or a challenge would leave Sysco carrying rate-lock losses and bridge costs ($54M rate-lock loss and $30M bridge amortization already recorded) without the deal [1][5]
Restaurant traffic softness plus fuel and sourcing pressures that consensus expects to hold fiscal Q1 2027 EPS growth near ~1.7%, against a 2.08% net margin that magnifies any cost shock [2][3]
